_comment: Room names and descriptions for area/hyrule.are, read by scripts/build_hyrule_area.py.
overworld: keyed by manifest coordinate. dungeons: "L<level>:<coordinate>", and
"L<level>:cellar:<coordinate>" for the block-stair cellar under that room; the generator
prefixes dungeon names with "Level N: ". special: the named caves, and one entry per cave
keyed "<kind>:<guide coordinate>" (rupee, shop, potion_shop, door_repair, gamble,
warp_hall, take_any, hint), so no two caves share text.
Descriptions are one paragraph each; the generator wraps them at 75 columns.

A1.name: Southwest Meadow
A1.description: A wide meadow of tall grass and yellow flowers fills the far southwest corner of the land, hemmed in by brown rock to the south and west. Some flower heads spin on their stalks with no wind to turn them. In the western rock a cave mouth stands open, a thread of smoke curling from it and steps leading down into firelight. It is a quiet, forgotten corner, and the only trampled path leads east toward the woods.

B1.name: Woodland Rock Face
B1.description: Trees crowd against the wall of brown rock that marks the southern edge of the land, their roots wedged into every crack. Crude stone-headed arrows lie snapped in the turf, and doglike pawprints circle a trampled patch of grass. One stretch of the rock face is crazed with fine cracks spreading from a hollow-sounding center, as if a bomb could open it. Paths lead north, east and west through the woods.

C1.name: Southern Woods
C1.description: Old trees stand in rows along the southern edge of the land, set as evenly as an orchard, their crowns meeting overhead in a leafy roof. The leaf mould is churned by heavy, clawed feet and littered with broken spear shafts and gnawed bones where something doglike has made camp. Somewhere among the trunks a twig cracks. Paths lead north, east and west.

D1.name: Path to the Manji
D1.description: A narrow trail winds east through the southern forest toward a ring of trees that grow in a pattern too regular to be natural, set like spokes around a hub. The birdsong fades and the air grows cooler the farther east the path goes, and snapped spears in the grass show the way is patrolled. Other trails branch north and west into the deeper forest.

E1.name: Grove of the Manji
E1.description: A ring of tall trees encloses a hushed clearing, and at its center a squat stone entrance is carved with a turning four-armed cross, the sign of the Manji. Cold air breathes out of the doorway, smelling of moss and damp stone. Deep paired dents in the turf show where something long-legged lands after each leap. Rock walls the clearing south and east, and the only way out is west.

F1.name: Sandy Glade
F1.description: A clearing of loose, pale sand opens among the trees, oddly bare where the forest should be. The sand is rippled and pocked with small round burrow holes, and every so often a patch of it heaves and spins as though something were boring up from below. At the glade's edge a low cave mouth opens in a bank, with steps leading down toward firelight. Paths lead north into the woods and east toward the hills.

G1.name: Crags West of the Start
G1.description: Brown rock juts up in jagged ridges just west of a quiet green field, the ground between them dented in pairs where some long-legged hopping thing lands hard and springs away again. One rock face is cracked and weak, and a faint rattle like dice in a cup seems to come from behind it, as if a bomb would open the way to somebody's game. Paths lead north, east toward the start, and west into the woods.

H1.name: The First Quest Begins
H1.description: A small green field lies at the foot of rocky brown hills, quiet and sunny, the grass trampled into a faint path. In the cliff to the north a dark cave mouth opens, and from within flickers the warm glow of twin fires. Someone has scratched a few plain words into the rock beside it: IT'S DANGEROUS TO GO ALONE. Paths lead north, east and west into the wider world.

I1.name: Meadow East of the Cave
I1.description: Open grassland stretches east from the starting hills, dotted with small boulders and clumps of green bushes. Round pebbles lie strewn across the grass, some still wet, as though spat from a mouth that lives here. One bush beside the rocks is dry and brittle, its leaves curling brown, plainly ready to burn, and a bitter smell of herbs hangs about it. Paths lead north, east and west.

J1.name: Stone Field
J1.description: A field of jumbled grey and brown boulders sprawls along the southern edge of the land, grass growing in tufts between them. One great stone sits loose in its bed, ringed by fresh-turned earth and too heavy for any ordinary arm, as if a bracelet of strength were needed to shift it aside. Paired dents mark where hopping things have landed among the rocks. The field opens east and west.

K1.name: Rocky Southern Ridge
K1.description: A rocky ridge runs along the southern edge of the land, brown stone breaking through thin, wind-flattened grass. The ground is scuffed with odd paired footprints that appear and vanish again several paces on, as if whatever made them leapt from boulder to boulder on long jointed legs. The scuffs are blue with crushed lichen. Trails follow the ridge east and west.

L1.name: Southern Sands
L1.description: Sandy ground stretches along the southern edge of the land, rippled by the wind and pocked with burrow holes that open and close like breathing. Now and then a spinning red shape bores up through the sand and sinks away again. To the south rises a rock wall, and one section of it is cracked and weak, the crackle of a pair of fires sounding faintly behind it as though a bomb might open a room. Paths lead north, east and west.

M1.name: Leever Dunes
M1.description: Low dunes of pale sand roll along the southern edge of the land, shifting and hissing whenever the wind picks up. Little whorls in the sand mark where something has spun itself down out of sight. A cracked face of rock rises at one side, and the clink of coins being stacked seems to echo behind it, as though a bomb might open somebody's game. Paths lead east and west.

N1.name: Southern Shore Path
N1.description: A grassy path runs along the southern edge of the land, the low boom of the sea drifting in from the east. Beside it rises a wall of brown rock, and one section is cracked and crumbling, hollow-sounding when the wind moans past. Whoever lives behind it, a bomb would make a door, and a door would have to be paid for. Small blue-grey stones lie scattered in the grass. Paths lead east and west.

O1.name: Southeast Grassland
O1.description: Wide grassland sweeps toward the southeastern coast, the long grass bent flat by a constant wind that carries salt from the sea. Small round stones lie scattered about, some half buried as if spat with force from a snout, and the turf is torn where something stout and eight-legged scuttles. Gulls cry somewhere to the east. Paths lead east toward the shore and west across the grass.

P1.name: Southeast Coast
P1.description: The land ends at a rocky shore in the far southeastern corner of Hyrule, where grey waves crash and white spray drifts on the wind. Tide pools glimmer among the tumbled rocks, and blue-grey stones lie flung far up the beach where no wave could have thrown them. It is the very end of the world in two directions. Paths lead north along the coast and west inland.

A2.name: Western Meadow Edge
A2.description: Open meadow runs right up to the western edge of the land, where the grass stops at a sheer brown bluff. A spinning flower rises and falls on the wind, and deep, heavy hoofprints cut through the blossoms beside scorched patches of grass, the trail of something large, four-legged and fire-breathing that patrols here. Paths lead north toward the rocks and east into the woods.

B2.name: The Tangled Woods
B2.description: Dense trees crowd close on every side, their branches knotted overhead into a dim green roof. Paths wind away in all four directions between the trunks, and the only sounds are rustling leaves and the creak of old wood. Snapped spear-shafts and blue-dyed scraps of hide lie half-buried in the leaf litter, dropped by whatever hunts these woods in pairs.

C2.name: Old Forest Clearing
C2.description: A hushed clearing opens among ancient oaks, their bark gnarled and split with age and their roots heaving up the soil. Fallen leaves lie ankle deep and smell of rain. At one edge a single bush has withered to a dry, papery brown, oddly lifeless beside the green, and the earth under it rings hollow, as though a fire might uncover something kept there. Trails wander away in every direction.

D2.name: Bramble Wood
D2.description: Thorny brambles crowd between the trunks, snagging cloth and skin alike, and the trail weaves a careful line through them. A bush beside the path has dried out completely, its leaves brittle and grey, and the ground behind it rings faintly hollow underfoot. Spat stones and spear shafts lie together in the thorns. Paths break away through the brambles in all four directions.

E2.name: The Lost Woods
E2.description: Every trunk here looks like every other, and the paths twist so strangely that a traveller can walk out one side of the grove and find the same trees waiting. Someone has cut a line into the bark of the oldest oak: NORTH, WEST, SOUTH, WEST. A cave mouth above the trail breathes a bitter smell of simmering herbs, and near the path a lone dead bush stands brittle enough to catch from a single spark.

F2.name: Forest Stream
F2.description: A narrow stream threads through the trees, chattering over pebbles and pooling in quiet, fern-hung basins. Mossy stepping stones make for an easy crossing, though now and then the water bulges and a scaly head breaks the surface to spit a ball of fire before sinking again. Scorch marks blister the stones. Cool air rises off the current, and paths lead away in all four directions.

G2.name: Candle Shop Knoll
G2.description: A grassy knoll rises above the surrounding fields, crowned by a weathered outcrop of brown rock. A cave mouth in its side flickers with a soft yellow glow, and the warm smell of melted wax hangs about the entrance, where a merchant trades in light against the dark places of the world. Pebbles lie scattered over the slope as if hurled from somewhere. Paths lead east, west and south.

H2.name: Rock Wall Above the Start
H2.description: A wall of brown rock rises along the north side of a grassy field, its face scarred and cracked. One section looks weaker than the rest, a hollow knock answering any tap on it, as if a bomb might break it open on somebody's hidden savings. Red-flecked pebbles lie spat across the grass. Trails lead east and west, and south toward the cave in the hills where the quest begins.

I2.name: Bush Row
I2.description: A tidy line of thick green bushes borders a sunny field, almost like a hedge someone once planted and forgot. One of them stands out from its neighbours, dry and brittle, its leaves browned and curled as though it would go up in flame in an instant, and a new-looking doorframe peeks between its roots. Worn paths cross the field to the north, south, east and west.

J2.name: River Bend
J2.description: A broad river swings through open country here, its water deep and green beneath an undercut, rocky bank. Reeds grow thick along the edge and dragonflies skim the shallows. Every so often the surface bulges, a finned head rises with a burning glow in its throat, and a wake slides away downstream. Dry ground leads north, east and west along the curve.

K2.name: Riverbank Thicket
K2.description: Dense bushes crowd the riverbank, their roots trailing into the slow brown water and their branches heavy with river mist. Among all that green one bush stands dry and dead, its twigs grey and snapping in the breeze, as though waiting for a spark, and someone has nailed a little ledger-board to its trunk. The water swirls where something lurks. Muddy paths lead north, east and west.

L2.name: Shaded Grove
L2.description: Tall elms cast deep, cool shade over a quiet grove carpeted in soft moss, and the birdsong falls silent more often than it should. Near the path one bush has withered entirely, its brown leaves rattling like paper in the faintest breeze, and the moss around it is worn by feet that came and went with full pockets. The grove opens onto trails heading north, south, east and west.

M2.name: Dark Pine Stand
M2.description: Dark pines grow shoulder to shoulder, their needles thick and springy underfoot and their branches blotting out much of the sky. The still air smells of resin and old woodsmoke, and crude spear marks score several trunks at chest height where something doglike practises its throw. Red-dyed rags hang from a broken branch. Narrow trails lead north, east and west between the trees.

N2.name: The Lion's Thicket
N2.description: A quiet clearing in the eastern forest is empty but for a single bush standing apart, dry and brittle and rooted in strangely flat, square-cut stone. Cold air seeps up from beneath its roots, carrying a smell of old masonry and deep places, and the carved paw of some great stone lion shows through the grass beside it. A spark would clear the way. Paths lead north, east and west.

O2.name: Eastern Wood Path
O2.description: A narrow trail runs east and west through a light, airy wood, sunlight dappling the ground between slender birches. Small round stones lie scattered along the track, some half buried as if they struck with force, and spear shafts lie broken among them. From the east comes the steady hush of waves and a faint tang of salt on the breeze.

P2.name: Coastal Shop Cave
P2.description: Grassy bluffs overlook the eastern sea, where long grey waves break white on the rocks below. In a rocky bank set back from the cliff edge a cave mouth opens, and a sharp whiff of black powder and lamp oil drifts out to mingle with the salt air, the smell of a merchant who sells bombs and arrows. The coast path runs north and south, and a track heads inland to the west.

A3.name: Western Crags
A3.description: Brown boulders and jagged rock spurs crowd the western edge of the world, and deep claw marks score the stone beside blackened streaks where something spat fire. Scattered bones bleach in the sun. To the north a channel of dark water cuts off the way, wide enough that only a raft could cross it, while a rough path winds south between the rocks.

B3.name: Deepwood Corner
B3.description: Old trees grow so close here that their canopy blots out the sky, leaving the forest floor in green gloom. Paths of trampled earth wind east and south between the trunks, past spear shafts snapped and left to rot. One bush near the trail is dry and brittle, its leaves brown and curling, and the soil beneath it is scuffed as if someone small comes and goes.

C3.name: Lost Woods Crossing
C3.description: The forest closes in on all sides, every trunk looking much like the next, and paths wander off in all four directions. Owls call in the shadows, and the moss grows on whichever side of the trees it pleases, no help to anyone lost. Deep doglike prints in red and blue mud cross the trail. To the north the trees begin to thin around a still, bright clearing.

D3.name: The Fairy Path
D3.description: A narrow, mossy trail winds between the trees, and here and there a faint glimmer of light seems to dance ahead to the north, where a spring is said to mend any wound. The rest of the woods is dim and muffled, its leaves trodden flat by heavy feet and scattered with broken spear shafts. Paths lead off in every direction.

E3.name: Forest River Ford
E3.description: A swift river splashes over a stony ford in the middle of the woods, cold and clear. The banks are slick with mud and covered in wet prints, and a sudden ripple now and then betrays a finned head that rises, spits a glowing ball, and slips under again. Spat pebbles litter the shallows. Paths lead on in all four directions.

F3.name: Shore Below the Snake
F3.description: The forest gives way to the western waters of Lake Hylia, glittering under an open sky. A small island rises a short distance to the north, and a dark serpent-shaped doorway can just be glimpsed on it across a channel too wide to step and narrow enough to bridge with a ladder. Paths lead east, west and south along the shore, where the water sometimes spits fire.

G3.name: Lake Hylia, Southwest Bank
G3.description: Grassy banks slope down to the water's edge, where cattails sway and dragonflies hover. Out on the lake a scaly head breaks the surface, glowing at the throat, and sinks again. A single dry bush grows near the path, ready to catch the slightest spark, and the turf around it is worn as though someone small and secretive lives under it. Trails lead north, east and west.

H3.name: Lakeside Meadow
H3.description: A pleasant open meadow stretches out beneath the sky, the grass short and green and dotted with wildflowers. Small red-flecked stones lie scattered about as though spat from somewhere, and the turf is torn by stubby, scuttling feet. The sound of lapping water drifts from the great lake to the north. The meadow runs on east and west.

I3.name: Crossroads South of the Lake
I3.description: Two worn dirt roads cross in the middle of open green country, rutted by cart wheels and dotted with spat stones. To the north the ground slopes down toward the sandy shore of Lake Hylia, and the smell of water hangs in the air. A rough milestone at the crossing points every way at once. The roads lead off in all four directions across the grass.

J3.name: Flower Field
J3.description: A wide field of tall grass and bright flowers sways in the wind, humming with bees. Overhead there is a strange whirring, and every so often a great flower lifts from its stalk, spinning like a top, and sails across the field before dropping back into the grass as if nothing had happened. The field is open on every side, with paths heading north, south, east and west.

K3.name: Rolling Green Downs
K3.description: Gentle green hills roll away beneath a broad sky, broken only by a few low rocks and scrubby bushes. The grass is pocked with small craters where stones have struck it hard, and a trail of stubby, eight-legged tracks leads from each one back toward a hollow in the turf. Paths lead east, west and south over the hills.

L3.name: Eastwood Glade
L3.description: A sunny glade sits in a ring of tall trees, the ground churned by heavy, clawed feet. Broken spear shafts lie in the long grass beside a cold firepit ringed with gnawed bones. One bush at the edge of the glade is as dry as old straw, and a small trodden path leads right up to its roots and stops. Ways lead out in every direction.

M3.name: Pinewood Rise
M3.description: Tall pines climb a gentle slope, their needles thick and soft underfoot and their sap sharp in the air. Muddy tracks of something large and dog-headed criss-cross the trail, and spear points have been sharpened on a flat rock until it shines. Scraps of blue hide hang from a low branch. Paths lead east, west and south through the trees.

N3.name: Moblin Hollow
N3.description: A shallow hollow among the trees is strewn with trampled grass, chewed bones and the ashes of a cold campfire. Crude spears lean against a fallen log, and the forest is noisy with snapping twigs and distant, piggish grunts. The ground is churned by broad, clawed feet. Paths climb out of the hollow in all four directions.

O3.name: Candlemaker's Dead End
O3.description: The forest trail runs out in a small hollow walled in by trees and a shoulder of grey rock. In the rock face a low cave mouth glows with a warm, steady flicker, and the smell of tallow and wick smoke drifts out on the still air, where a merchant sells candles and bait to those who come this far. The woods beyond are too thick to pass, so the only way back is west.

P3.name: The Coast's Lonely Ledge
P3.description: Rough grass runs down to the eastern shore, where the sea washes against tumbled rocks. Just offshore a small flat ledge of stone sits alone above the waves, separated from the land by a strip of water too wide to step and narrow enough to bridge with a ladder. A faint red glow pulses on the ledge like a heartbeat. The coast path leads north and south.

A4.name: The Graveyard's Southern Fence
A4.description: Weathered headstones lean in crooked rows behind a low, crumbling wall, their names long since rubbed away by wind and rain. The grass grows thin and grey, a cold mist clings to the ground, and now and then a pale shape drifts across the stones and is gone. To the south the land drops to dark water and a small stone landing for a raft, and open country runs on to the east and north.

B4.name: Hollow of Headstones
B4.description: A sunken hollow of cracked gravestones sits under a sky that never quite seems to brighten. Crows' feathers and old wilted flowers litter the bare earth between the graves, and the air smells of damp soil. The mist here gathers itself into shapes that drift between the stones, and touching a grave seems to wake them. The burial ground climbs north, while a worn path slips out west.

C4.name: The Still Pond
C4.description: A ring of tall dark trees closes in around a round, perfectly still pond, its surface black and glassy, and no fairy has ever danced over it. Smooth carved stones edge the water as though something was built beneath it long ago. Old folk say there are secrets where fairies do not live, and that a certain tune can make even sleeping water draw back. The only way out is the forest track to the south.

D4.name: Fairy Pond of the Woods
D4.description: The forest opens onto a bright, clear pool fed by a quiet spring, its banks soft with moss and tiny white flowers. Motes of light drift and spin over the water like fairies at play, and the air feels warm and restful, as if every wound and weariness drains away into it. A narrow track leads back south into the trees.

E4.name: Riverside Cave
E4.description: A swift green river cuts through the woods here, its banks lined with reeds and smooth grey stones. Across a stretch of grass a low cave mouth is set into a rocky bank, and the whiff of black powder drifting from inside marks a merchant of bombs and arrows. A finned head rises from the water now and then, spits a glowing ball, and sinks. Trails follow the river north and south.

F4.name: Isle of the Snake
F4.description: A small green island rises out of the lake, ringed on every side by cold, lapping water. At its heart a dark stone entrance is carved in the coiled shape of a serpent, its doorway breathing out damp air. Across a gap of water to the south lies the lakeshore, too wide to jump; only those who came over on a raft or bridged it with a ladder ever set foot on its grass.

G4.name: Lake Hylia, Western Reeds
G4.description: Tall reeds rustle along the western edge of Lake Hylia, and the water slaps gently against a muddy bank. A finned head sometimes rises out of the reeds to spit fire, then sinks. A lone, scraggly bush stands somewhat apart from the rest, dry and brittle as tinder, and a merchant's painted price mark shows on a stone among its roots. The shore curves away east, and a path climbs south.

H4.name: Lake Hylia, South Shore
H4.description: Broad blue water stretches north as far as the eye can see, sparkling under an open sky, its far shore lost in haze. Ripples spread from somewhere out in the deep, where something finned rises and sinks. Near the bank a single dense bush grows by itself, dry and crackling in the sun, and two thin threads of smoke rise through its roots as if fires burned somewhere below. The shore runs on east and west.

I4.name: Lake Hylia Sand Bar
I4.description: A pale sand bar runs along the lake's edge, the sand rippled and pocked with burrow holes from which a red spinning thing sometimes bores up. The water laps in long slow waves, and a lonely bush stands at the edge of the grass, brittle and brown, with coin-sized footprints worn around it. Paths lead north along the water, south toward the fields and west along the shore.

J4.name: Boulder Meadow
J4.description: Rolling green meadow is broken by heavy grey boulders that lie half sunk in the turf. One sits a little apart from the others, as if it had been rolled there by some great hand and might be rolled away again by a strong enough one, and a draught breathes up from the earth at its base. Spat stones lie about the grass. Trails lead off to the north, east and south.

K4.name: Craggy Rise
K4.description: Brown rock juts up through the grass in jagged ridges, and loose stones skitter down the slopes at every gust. The soil is scuffed with the paired prints of long-legged hopping things, blue lichen crushed into each one. Tucked under one ledge is a dark cave mouth that smells of black powder, where a merchant trades bombs and arrows. Paths run north, east and west.

L4.name: Eastern Thicket
L4.description: Dense trees crowd together here, their roots knotting across a narrow trail littered with snapped arrows and gnawed bones. One bush near the path looks unusually dry, its leaves curled and ready to catch the smallest spark, and a sweet, bitter smell of medicine drifts from beneath it. Red-dyed hide hangs on a thornbush. The thicket opens to the north, the south and the west.

M4.name: The Eastern Dock
M4.description: A weathered wooden dock juts out from the grassy bank over open water, its planks bleached grey and its posts green with weed. Water stretches away northward toward a hazy green spit where a stone gate stands, too far to swim but easy going on a raft. Spat stones lie scattered on the planks. Behind the dock the meadow rolls off to the east.

N4.name: Wooded Crossroads
N4.description: Four forest paths meet in a small trampled clearing ringed by stout trees. Broken spearheads and torn bits of blue hide lie in the leaf litter. A single bush at the clearing's edge has dried out completely, its twigs as brittle as kindling, and through them the glint of a polished shield seems to catch the light from somewhere below. Ways lead off in every direction.

O4.name: Armos Sentinel Grove
O4.description: Stone knight statues stand in silent rows among the trees, shields raised and faces worn smooth by the years. They seem to watch the path, and one stands slightly out of line with the others, the moss on its base torn as if it had stepped down and back again. Touching any of them feels like a dare. The grove is a dead end, and the only way out leads back west.

P4.name: Eastern Cliffs
P4.description: The land ends abruptly at a line of rocky cliffs above the sea, and salt spray drifts up on a cool wind. Gulls wheel and cry overhead while waves boom against the rocks far below. Blue-grey stones lie flung across the clifftop where something stout spits them at passers-by. A grassy track runs along the clifftop to the north and south.

A5.name: The Graveyard, Lower Rows
A5.description: The southern rows of the graveyard are crowded with weathered headstones, their names long worn away and their tops green with lichen. Dead grass crackles underfoot, and a cold mist clings to the ground between the graves, gathering now and then into a pale, drifting shape that fades when looked at squarely. The paths lead north into the older graves, south along the fence and east toward the living lands.

B5.name: The Graveyard Gate
B5.description: Here the graves thin out toward the edge of the burial ground, where a gap in the boundary lets travellers pass. The headstones nearest the gate lean outward as if to see who comes and goes, and the earth before each one is disturbed, as though touching a grave wakes whatever sleeps beneath. The mist gathers thickest by the gap. Ways lead north, south, east and west.

C5.name: Ghost Hill
C5.description: A low grassy hill overlooks the graveyard to the west, its slopes dotted with wildflowers and scarred by heavy hoofprints and black scorch marks where something breathes fire. A flower head spins up from the grass now and then and whirls away. The air is warmer than among the graves. A crevice to the north needs a ladder to cross, and the way continues east and west.

D5.name: The Cracked Bluff
D5.description: A tall bluff of brown rock stands at the edge of the highlands, its face stained by old water. Near its base the stone is cracked and flaking, and a faint herbal scent of boiled roots drifts out of the gaps, as if a medicine woman kept shop behind a wall that a bomb could open. A narrow crevice to the north wants a ladder, and the land opens to the west.

E5.name: The Silent Sentinels
E5.description: A cluster of stone soldiers stands guard on a patch of sandy ground, raised in two rows like an honour guard. The sand around them is restless and churns in small spirals. The middle statue of the top row stands a little apart from the others, its base scuffed as if it had shifted, and a faint blue gleam like a jewelled ring seems to shine from beneath it. The only way out leads south.

F5.name: The Quiet Glade
F5.description: Tall trees ring a peaceful glade of soft grass, and the light falls in gentle patches through their leaves. Birdsong drifts from the branches, and no tracks but a deer's cross the turf. A narrow gully leads north toward the higher country, too deep to climb without a ladder, and the glade opens to the east.

G5.name: The Sheltered Hollow
G5.description: A hollow is tucked between low hills, sheltered from the wind and quiet. Green grass grows thick and undisturbed, and a few old trees stand at its edges, their roots knotted over smooth river stones. It is one of the few places in Hyrule where no claw or snout has marked the ground. Paths lead north and west, and the stillness feels like a held breath.

H5.name: The Eagle's Gate
H5.description: On a spit of green land cut off by the river, a stone entrance stands in a rocky outcrop, its lintel carved with the spread wings of an eagle and walled about by green-grey statues. Cool, musty air drifts from the darkness within, smelling of bats. The river runs wide to the east, where a wooden dock waits for anyone with a raft to cross back.

I5.name: The River Landing
I5.description: The river widens here, and a sturdy wooden dock juts out from the bank into the current. Across the water to the west a green shore with a carved stone gate waits, unreachable on foot but an easy crossing by raft. Spat stones of two colours litter the planks. Grass grows thick along the bank, and the land opens to the north and south.

J5.name: The Fairy Fountain, North
J5.description: A clear pool lies in a ring of soft grass and white stones, its surface glittering with tiny motes of light that flit and circle like fairies at play. The water is perfectly still and smells of rain and flowers, and a warmth rises from it that eases every ache and closes every wound. A path leads away to the south.

K5.name: The Peahat Fields
K5.description: Wide fields of grass and wildflowers stretch out under an open sky. Some of the flowers spin and lift from their stalks as though caught in a private wind, whirl across the field, and settle again, and they are said to be soft only while they rest. Patches of blue-grey sand show through the turf where something burrows. Paths lead off to the north, east and south.

L5.name: The Blowing Sands
L5.description: Sand drifts across this stretch of the field in long, low ridges, burying the grass in places. Small mounds appear and vanish as something spins up from beneath and bores down again, and the wind lifts fine grit that stings the eyes. A rusty arrowhead lies half buried, lost by someone who did not stay. The way leads north, south and west.

M5.name: The Moon Gate
M5.description: A stone entrance stands near the water's edge, its doorway crowned with a carved crescent moon and its steps worn smooth by the lake's damp. Air drifts from inside, smelling of stone, old water and shed snakeskin. The lake's edge cuts off the south, where a wooden dock juts into the water for those who came by raft.

N5.name: The Armos Shore
N5.description: A row of stone soldiers stands on a grassy rise above the lake, shields set and faces blank. One statue stands slightly apart from the others, its base scuffed and cracked as if it had moved, and the grass around it is flattened by heavy stone feet. Something hidden beneath it rattles like loose coin. Paths lead north and south along the shore.

O5.name: The Octorok Banks
O5.description: The grassy bank slopes gently to the water's edge, scattered with spat stones of red and blue and the round, stubby prints of things that scuttle and spit. The lake glitters to the south and east, and reeds rustle wherever the water meets the grass. A path leads east along the shore and north toward the cliffs.

P5.name: Lake Hylia, Eastern Dock
P5.description: A wooden dock reaches out into Lake Hylia from the eastern shore, and across the water to the north a small green island sits alone. The water is deep and dark near the dock, and bubbles rise from beneath it before a finned head surfaces to spit fire. Only a raft could carry anyone north from here; the shore continues south and west.

A6.name: The Old Graveyard
A6.description: Row upon row of grey headstones stand in the cold earth, many tilted and half sunk, laid out in a grid so regular the dead seem to stand in ranks. The grass between them is withered, and a chill hangs in the air that the sun cannot burn off. Thin mist curls around the stones and sometimes rises into a pale, grinning shape. Paths lead east and south.

B6.name: The Hero's Grave
B6.description: The graveyard reaches its oldest corner here, where the headstones are tallest and most worn. One grave sits apart, its stone askew on a slab that looks as if it could be shifted, and the cold is deepest beside it. Faint letters on the headstone read: THE THIEF TOOK ONE BLADE. ANOTHER SLEEPS BELOW FOR ONE STRONG ENOUGH TO WAKE IT. The dead seem restless all around. Paths lead south and west.

C6.name: The Dragon's Gate
C6.description: Bare highland rock surrounds a dark entrance carved into a low outcrop, its mouth framed by stone shaped like the head and coiled body of a dragon. Hot, stale air breathes out of it. Deep hoofprints and blackened scorch marks from something that spits fire cover the ground, and a narrow crevice to the south is the only way out, crossed with a ladder.

D6.name: The Western Warp Stone
D6.description: A lonely boulder sits in a ring of trampled grass, heavier and squarer than the stones around it, far too heavy to move without a bracelet of great strength. The earth at its base is scraped, as if a stair beneath had been uncovered and covered again. Deep hoofprints circle the place, and a narrow crevice drops away to the south. The way east lies open.

E6.name: The Armos Gallery
E6.description: A row of carved stone soldiers stands at attention across the highland, each holding a spear, their blank eyes fixed on the horizon. They look patient and very old. One of them, the second from the end, stands slightly off true from the others, and the ground beneath it rings hollow, as though it guards some small treasure. A crevice to the north leads toward the mountain.

F6.name: The Bomb Merchant's Cave
F6.description: Flowers carpet this open field, some of them spinning on their stalks, and a cave mouth yawns in a low rock face at its western side. A smell of black powder and burnt fuses lingers at the entrance, where bombs and arrows are sold by the dozen. Narrow crevices cut the land to the north and south, and the way west lies open.

G6.name: The Meadow Bluff
G6.description: A grassy meadow runs up against a weathered bluff, bright with wildflowers that sway and whirl in the breeze. Part of the bluff's face is fractured and loose, with a faint draught slipping through the cracks and the glint of polished metal beyond them, as though a shieldsmith kept a shop that only a bomb could open. The meadow opens to the east and slopes down to the south.

H6.name: Foot of Death Mountain
H6.description: Here the green fields meet the brown flanks of Death Mountain, and a path climbs northward into the boulders toward peaks that smoke against the sky. Flowers grow thick along the trail, some of them spinning as if alive. In a rocky outcrop beside the path one section is cracked and crumbling, and a bitter herbal scent drifts from somewhere behind it. Ways lead north, east and west.

I6.name: The Withered Thicket
I6.description: Open grassland is broken here by clusters of dry, scrubby bushes. One bush stands alone, its branches brittle and dead, and it looks as if a single spark would set it ablaze; the turf at its roots is worn by small feet that come and go with something heavy. Blackened twigs and old ash lie scattered about. The field opens to the east, south and west.

J6.name: The Sandy Flats
J6.description: The grass gives way to a stretch of pale, shifting sand, warm underfoot and strangely restless. Small mounds rise and sink across it, and every so often a red shape spins up out of the ground, bores along a few paces, and dives back down. The flats run east and west, and the air shimmers with heat.

K6.name: The Dune Strip
K6.description: A long strip of dunes runs between the green fields and the mountains, the sand rippled into fine waves by the wind. Spiral burrow marks appear and fade across it, the dust in them faintly blue. The way leads east, west and south, and the brown peaks of Death Mountain loom to the north, smoking at their crowns.

L6.name: Below the Lost Hills
L6.description: Sand and scrub mingle at the foot of the rolling hills to the north, where a narrow crevice climbs toward them that only a ladder will bridge. The ground is soft and pocked with burrow holes, and a flower spins lazily overhead. Paths lead off in every direction, and the hills above seem to shift whenever you look away.

M6.name: Lake Hylia, North Cliffs
M6.description: Brown cliffs rise from the northern edge of Lake Hylia, and the blue water glints below. The rock is dented by paired springing marks, and one part of the cliff face is split with deep cracks, firelight flickering behind them beside a slower red pulse, as though a bomb would open a room where a heart and a potion wait and only one may be taken. A crevice leads north; the shore runs east and west.

N6.name: Lake Hylia, North Shore
N6.description: Green grass runs down to the lake's northern shore, where small waves lap at a strip of pebbles. Spat stones lie scattered on the turf. A low rock face at the back of the shore is cracked through in one place, and coins seem to chink behind it whenever the wind gusts. A narrow crevice leads north into the mountains, and paths run east, west and south.

O6.name: Lake Hylia, Northeast Shore
O6.description: The shore curves here around a broad sweep of Lake Hylia, the water deep and dark close to the bank. Bubbles rise now and then from beneath the surface, and once in a while a finned, fishlike head rises after them to spit a glowing ball across the grass. Tufts of grass fringe the rocks, and the shoreline continues west and south.

P6.name: The Lonely Isle
P6.description: A small island sits alone in the eastern waters of Lake Hylia, a patch of green grass ringed by blue, and at its middle a low cave mouth glows with firelight while a faint red pulse beats somewhere within. Waves slap gently at its edges. No path leads here except across the water, and the only way back is by a little dock on the southern side, where a raft can be put in.

A7.name: The Western Gorge
A7.description: Steep brown walls box in this gorge at the western edge of the mountains, and the wind funnels through with a low howl. Hoofprints and scorch marks cross and recross the floor. In one wall a crack spreads like a spider's web, and behind it the clack of a game being played seems to echo, as if a bomb would let a gambler in. Northward a deep crevice splits the rock; the way east is open.

B7.name: The Windswept Shelf
B7.description: A flat shelf of rock juts out from the mountainside, scoured clean by constant wind. A few tough flowers grow in the lee of the boulders, their petals torn ragged, and one of them spins as though it would fly. Deep hoofprints lead to the edge and back. A crevice runs along the northern side, and the only easy way off the shelf leads west.

C7.name: The Shieldmaker's Bluff
C7.description: A blunt bluff of brown stone rises from the slope, its face streaked with mineral stains and scorched by fiery breath. Low down, a section of it is cracked and loose, and the faint ring of a hammer on metal seems to come from somewhere inside, where shields are sold to those willing to blast their way in. The trail leads east, and a crevice opens in the rock to the north.

D7.name: Broken Stone Terrace
D7.description: Terraces of broken stone step down the mountainside like a ruined stair. Lynel tracks, deep and wide, scar the dust between them, and scorch marks show where they spat fire at shadows. At the back of one terrace the cliff is fissured and weak, as if hiding a hollow full of someone's coin. A crevice to the north separates this place from the heights; ways lead east and west.

E7.name: The Crumbling Scarp
E7.description: The scarp here is old and tired, its brown face slumping into heaps of rubble. One stretch looks ready to give way altogether, its cracks deep enough to whistle in the wind, and whoever lives behind it would no doubt charge for the door. Scorch marks blacken the boulders, and a narrow gully drops away to the south toward greener land. Ways lead east and west.

F7.name: Highland Overlook
F7.description: The mountain pauses here in a high meadow of thin grass and wildflowers, ringed by brown boulders. From its edge the whole of the western highlands spreads below, the graveyard grey in the distance. Hoofprints and a spinning flower or two share the meadow. The wind carries the scent of the lowlands up the slope, and crevices break the ground to north and south.

G7.name: The Rumbling Gully
G7.description: A gully runs east and west beneath an unstable cliff, and every few moments a rock tumbles from above and bounds across it, bouncing high before it shatters. Gravel crunches underfoot. One section of the gully wall is split with fresh cracks, and a faint clink, like coins being counted for a wager, seems to echo behind it.

H7.name: The Lost Hills
H7.description: Brown hills rise and fall here, each fold of ground so like the last that the eye loses its place among them. The trail climbs north toward the high peaks between banks of loose scree, and paths wander off east and west along the slope. On a flat stone by the trail someone has scratched: GO UP, UP, THE MOUNTAIN AHEAD. Loose rocks bound down from above now and then.

I7.name: The Boulder Run
I7.description: Loose rocks careen down the mountainside and across this stretch of trail, bouncing in long arcs and leaving the path littered with splinters of stone. The cliffs on either side are scarred where boulders have struck them. Dust hangs in the air and the clatter never fully stops. The trail runs east and west, and a quick traveller keeps moving.

J7.name: Rolling Stone Ravine
J7.description: A shallow ravine runs east and west between walls of crumbling brown rock. Stones break free from the rim and roll down the slope in short, bouncing bursts, and gouges in the ravine floor mark their favourite paths. The air tastes of dust, and the rumble overhead never stops for long.

K7.name: The Springing Hills
K7.description: Rolling brown hills begin here, each one shaped so much like the last that the eye loses its place among them, the ground dented with paired springing marks. The river from the falls to the north tumbles over a rock face in a white curtain, and behind its spray a dark opening leads down into the cliff. A crevice divides the hills from the high country to the north, and paths run east and west.

L7.name: Hills Below the Basin
L7.description: Brown hills rise and fall in every direction here, scored by narrow crevices that cut the ground to the north and south and can only be crossed by ladder. The wind moans through the gaps between them like distant laughter, and loose stones skitter down the slopes at every gust. Paths wind east and west along the ridgelines.

M7.name: Lone Armos Ridge
M7.description: A single weathered stone soldier stands guard on this narrow ridge, its carved face worn smooth by the wind and its spear chipped at the point. Brown rock falls away on both sides. The ground around the statue is scuffed, as if it sometimes steps off its post, and warm air rises from a seam under its base, as though pushing it aside would uncover a stair. Gaps open north and south, and paths run east and west.

N7.name: The Heavy Boulder
N7.description: A small high meadow is ringed by boulders, and one of them sits a little apart from the rest, squarer and heavier, with a scraped track in the earth beside it as though it had once been moved by somebody wearing a bracelet of great strength. Flowers grow thick here, some spinning in the wind. Crevices lead north and south, and paths run east and west.

O7.name: The Scarred Cliffs
O7.description: These cliffs are pocked and gouged, and one patch in particular is laced with cracks so deep that light seems to show between them, as though a bomb would open a room someone else would want paid for. Paired springing marks dent the dusty ground. The way runs east and west along the base of the rock, and a crevice opens to the north.

P7.name: The Eastern Cliffs
P7.description: The mountains drop sharply to the east here, and a broad shelf of rock catches the morning sun. A cave mouth opens in the cliff, and from its shadow comes the rattle of something being shaken, then laughter and a voice inviting all comers to play the money-making game. Wildflowers grow along the shelf, some of them spinning, and a crevice splits the rock to the north.

A8.name: Death Mountain's Western Summit
A8.description: The world ends here in a wall of brown boulders, stacked shoulder to shoulder against a pale, empty sky. Thin wind whistles through the gaps and carries nothing but grit and the distant clatter of falling rock. To the south a narrow crevice splits the stone, too wide to step across and too deep to see the bottom of without a ladder to bridge it. The way east follows the summit.

B8.name: Lynel Ridge
B8.description: A high ridge of rust-brown rock runs east and west, its ground churned by heavy hooves and dotted with scorched patches where something spat fire. One stretch of the cliff face is webbed with fine cracks, as though the stone behind it were hollow and lived in, and whoever lives there will want the door paid for. A deep crevice bars the way south.

C8.name: The High Boulder Pass
C8.description: Rounded boulders the size of huts crowd this pass, leaving a crooked lane of bare earth between them. The air is thin and cold, and every sound bounces back twice from the cliffs. Hoofprints the width of a shield and singed lichen mark the trail, and a sheer-sided crevice opens in the rock to the south. The pass runs east and west.

D8.name: Rockfall Crest
D8.description: Loose scree pours down from the peaks above, and every so often a fresh stone comes bounding across the crest with a hollow clatter. The ground is pocked with craters from earlier falls. In the northern cliff one patch of rock looks oddly brittle, flaking at a touch, as if a single bomb would open it, and a narrow crevice cuts the slope to the south. The crest runs west.

E8.name: The Medicine Woman's Ledge
E8.description: Walled in on three sides by brown crags, this quiet ledge opens only to the east. A dark cave mouth is set into the rock, its threshold swept clean, and a faint bitter smell of boiled herbs drifts out of it, the shop of a woman who sells medicine to those carrying a royal letter. The ground nearby is trampled by heavy hooves, and the wind moans over the rim.

F8.name: Spectacle Rock
F8.description: Two great round boulders stand side by side on the summit, joined by a low saddle of stone like a giant's pair of spectacles left on the mountaintop. Sand has blown into drifts between them. The left-hand rock sounds hollow and is seamed with hairline cracks, and the air near it is colder than it ought to be, as if the way to death itself lay behind. Paths lead east and west.

G8.name: East of Spectacle Rock
G8.description: A broad shelf of packed earth stretches between rows of brown boulders, the twin humps of Spectacle Rock just visible to the west. Wind-flattened weeds cling to the cracks, and a few hardy flowers nod in the gusts, one of them spinning. Scorched hoofprints cross the shelf. Far below, the green of Hyrule spreads out like a quilt. Paths lead east and west.

H8.name: The Summit Road
H8.description: A worn path threads east and west along the mountain's crown, hemmed in by tumbled boulders and scorched by fiery breath. One face of the cliff shows a dark crack running from top to bottom, as if a single bomb might open it on a room someone would charge for. To the south the trail stops at a narrow crevice with the mountain trail visible beyond.

I8.name: Avalanche Slope
I8.description: The mountain sheds itself constantly here. Rocks break loose from the heights and come bouncing down in long arcs, smashing into gravel on the boulders below. The path east and west is littered with shattered stone, the dust never quite settles, and the safest pace through is a run.

J8.name: Death Mountain's Dead End
J8.description: Boulders close in on every side but the west, forming a still, sheltered pocket at the top of the world. The silence is heavy after the clatter of the slopes, and not one fallen stone lies on the ground. Nothing grows here but grey lichen, the only marks in the dust are the wind's, and the way back is west.

K8.name: The White Sword Falls
K8.description: A river spills over the lip of the mountain and drops in a roaring white curtain, filling the air with cold spray and rainbows. At the very top of the climb a cave mouth opens in the rock beside the falls, half hidden by mist, and the stone around it is worn smooth by those who came to prove their strength. Ripples in the pool below suggest something finned moves beneath. A crevice lies south.

L8.name: The Lizard's Gate
L8.description: Beyond the confusing folds of the Lost Hills the ground levels into a hidden basin of reddish sand. At its heart a squat entrance is cut into the stone, framed in a carved shape like a crouching lizard, its doorway black and cool. Dry wind hisses through the sand where something red bores up and dives again, and a crevice bars the way back south.

M8.name: The Candle Merchant's Hollow
M8.description: A dip among the high boulders shelters a cave mouth from the worst of the wind. A whiff of tallow and lamp smoke hangs at the entrance, where candles and other goods are sold, and the dust before it is scuffed by many feet. Small craters show where something springs and lands, springs and lands, all across the hollow. Ways lead east, and a crevice lies south.

N8.name: Tektite Heights
N8.description: The rock here is pitted with shallow dents, as though something heavy had been bouncing across it on long legs for years. Brown cliffs rise to the north, and one section of them is cracked and crumbling, with a faint draught whispering out of the seams and a smell of bitter medicine on it. A narrow crevice divides the heights from the land to the south, and the way west is open.

O8.name: Ledge of the Letter Cave
O8.description: A lonely ledge looks out over the eastern slopes, with a cave mouth gaping in the cliff behind it. Inside, a warm glow flickers, as though a pair of fires were kept burning against the cold. Someone has chalked beside the entrance: SHOW THIS TO THE OLD WOMAN. The wind is softer here, and a crevice falls away to the south.

P8.name: The Northeast Crag
P8.description: The far corner of the mountains ends in a sheer brown crag above the eastern wilds, the eastmost point of Hyrule's high country. A dark cave opens in its base, small and easily overlooked, and over the entrance someone has scrawled: IT'S A SECRET TO EVERYBODY. Stubborn shrubs grow in the cracks, and a deep crevice to the south falls away into shadow.

L1:B1.name: West Guardroom
L1:B1.description: A plain square chamber of teal flagstones, its corners furred with dust and spattered with bat droppings. Something leathery has left fine scratches along the high ledges, and a faint, erratic flutter echoes from the ceiling, swooping and stopping and swooping again. Two stone eagles stand in the corners with their wings folded. The only way out is the open doorway east, back toward the entry.

L1:C1.name: Eagle Gate
L1:C1.description: Cold teal stone rises on every side of this first chamber, the walls carved with rows of grim, staring faces and a great eagle spreading its wings above the north door. Daylight from the stair behind fades within a few paces, and the air smells of wet rock and bats. Open doorways lead east and west, while the northern door is barred shut and fitted with a heavy iron keyhole.

L1:D1.name: East Bone Room
L1:D1.description: Bleached bone fragments lie scattered across the tiled floor of this chamber, and the air carries the dry, chalky smell of old marrow. Two squat stone blocks stand near the middle like plinths waiting for statues, their edges nicked by rusty sword blows. Now and then the bones seem to shift and click on their own. A single open doorway leads west to the entry.

L1:C2.name: Rattling Passage
L1:C2.description: A row of squat stone blocks runs across the middle of this chamber, dividing it into two narrow lanes. Bones have been kicked into the corners beside a dented shield and a notched sword, and a faint rattle lingers after every sound, like a skeleton jumping in place. A locked door with a brass-ringed keyhole leads south, back toward the gate, and an open arch leads north.

L1:B3.name: Shuttered West Room
L1:B3.description: A low-ceilinged chamber of chill teal stone, where bat droppings crust the tops of a few scattered blocks and a papery rustle drifts down from the dark. The air tastes of dust. A heavy iron shutter fills the eastern doorway, dropped by whatever magic keeps this dungeon's halls closed until they are cleared, and the north door is locked, its keyhole ringed with rust.

L1:C3.name: Diamond-Tiled Crossing
L1:C3.description: Four ways meet in this broad chamber, its floor laid in worn diamond-patterned tiles around a square of raised blocks. Bones and a broken shield lie in the corners. A heavy iron shutter is sunk into the western doorway, and open arches lead east and south. Part of the north wall is crazed with dark hairline fissures, as if a bomb might bring it down.

L1:D3.name: Keese-Fouled Gallery
L1:D3.description: The vaulted ceiling of this gallery vanishes into darkness, and the stale air is thick with the musk of roosting bats. Droppings crust the floor between low rows of raised blocks, the teal walls are streaked white beneath every ledge, and the rafters are scored with tiny claw marks. An open doorway leads west, and a patch of the north wall is cracked and sounds hollow, as if a bomb would open it.

L1:A4.name: Eagle's Ember Alcove
L1:A4.description: Teal flagstones run back to a squat pair of braziers whose flames burn low and patient, the kind tended by someone who expects few visitors. Between the fires the stone is rubbed pale by long standing, and soot has painted a soft grey shape like an eagle's wing up the wall behind them. The room is warm, still and oddly homely for a dungeon. A heavy iron shutter seals the eastern doorway.

L1:B4.name: Slime-Slick Hall
L1:B4.description: The flagstones here are tacky with a glistening film, and small wet smears wander across them where little blobs of jelly creep and hop. The smell is sour, like spoiled broth. One block in the middle of the floor sits askew, scraped as though pushing it works some hidden catch. A locked door leads south, an open archway leads east, and a heavy iron shutter fills the western doorway.

L1:C4.name: Chamber of Pillars
L1:C4.description: Square stone blocks march across this large chamber in a rigid grid, leaving narrow lanes between them, and gelatinous smears gleam on the tiles where something small and quivering hops from lane to lane. Open doorways lead north and west, a locked door with a keyhole bars the east, and the south wall is split by a dark web of cracks that a bomb would open.

L1:D4.name: Scarred Hall
L1:D4.description: Curved gouges and scuff marks score the walls at shoulder height, as if something has been flung against them again and again and caught on the way back: the mark of a thrown boomerang. Splinters of red-painted wood lie by the corners. An open doorway leads east, a locked door leads west, and the south wall is fractured and weak enough to bomb.

L1:E4.name: Hall of Grasping Walls
L1:E4.description: The walls of this chamber seem to press closer than they should, and dark handprints smudge the stone high up near the ceiling, as if great hands slid out of the walls to grab at passers-by. Long drag marks lead from the middle of the floor toward the stone. An open doorway leads west, while the north door is locked fast, its keyhole worn bright.

L1:C5.name: Ossuary Hall
L1:C5.description: Old bones lie heaped in drifts against the walls of this dim chamber, and a pair of stone blocks squats near its center beside a rusted sword stuck point-down in the grout. The faint clatter of something settling never quite stops. An open arch leads south, and a locked door with an iron keyhole stands to the north.

L1:E5.name: Hall of Threefold Scorches
L1:E5.description: Scorch marks blacken the floor of this long chamber, every blast fanning out in three paths from a raised ledge of stone at the eastern end, its lip gouged by heavy claws. The air is hot and stinks of sulphur and charred bone, and the teal tiles nearest the ledge have cracked in the heat. A locked door leads south, and the door east, marked with an eagle around its keyhole, opens only to the guardian's key.

L1:F5.name: Eagle's Golden Sanctum
L1:F5.description: Smooth teal stone encloses this small, hushed sanctum, its walls inlaid with a triangle within a triangle. A soft golden glow hangs in the air though nothing here burns, and above the floor turns a triangle of light that would carry a hero home. An iron-banded chest stands locked at the centre, and the heavy door west, back toward the dragon's lair, bears the eagle's mark around its keyhole.

L1:B6.name: Chamber of Blade Traps
L1:B6.description: Deep grooves run across the floor of this chamber from its corners, polished smooth by spiked blades that rest against the walls and shoot toward anyone who crosses their line, then slide back. A single stone block in the middle sits a little askew, its base scraped as though it has been shifted before and something lies beneath. A locked door leads east.

L1:C6.name: Northern Guardroom
L1:C6.description: Curved scuff marks and dents pock the walls of this high northern chamber, and the floor is littered with chips of broken stone and the splinters of a thrown boomerang. Cold air drifts down from cracks in the vaulted ceiling, and a pair of eagle statues glares from the corners. Locked doors with heavy keyholes stand to the south and to the west.

L1:cellar:B6.name: Undercroft of Brick Ledges
L1:cellar:B6.description: A narrow ladder drops into a long basement of brick ledges and black gaps, the kind of place one crosses sideways, a ledge at a time. The air smells of turned earth and old candle stubs, and the lowest rung of the ladder is polished bright. Somebody's hoard of rupees was tucked on a stone shelf at the far end. The ladder climbs back up to the chamber above.

L2:B1.name: Crescent Gate
L2:B1.description: Pale blue stone surrounds this entrance hall, its walls carved with crescent moons worn soft by time and a pair of stone dragons crouched beside the doors. A chill draught spills down the stair behind, carrying the smell of the lake outside. Faint slither tracks cross the dust. Open doorways lead north and east into the darker halls beyond.

L2:C1.name: Shed Skin Chamber
L2:C1.description: Papery snake skins lie curled in the corners of this blue-walled chamber, and thin sinuous tracks wind through the dust, running straight and fast wherever they line up with a doorway, as if whatever made them charges anything that crosses its sight. Squat stone blocks frame the center of the room. An open doorway leads west to the entrance, and another leads north.

L2:A2.name: Coiled Track Room
L2:A2.description: A dead-end chamber on the dungeon's western edge, its dusty floor scored by long looping drag marks that suddenly straighten into furrows. The air is musty and faintly reptilian, and a dry rasp seems to come and go along the walls. A heavy iron shutter seals the only doorway, to the east, and it will not lift until the room is quiet.

L2:B2.name: Blue Antechamber
L2:B2.description: Stone blocks stand in two short rows across this chamber, and the blue walls sweat a faint chill. Shed scales gleam between the floor tiles like flakes of mica, and the dust is furrowed by quick, straight charges. Open doorways lead east and south toward the entrance, while the western door is a heavy iron shutter.

L2:C2.name: Moonstone Crossroads
L2:C2.description: Wide and echoing, this chamber sits where several halls meet, its tiles worn into shallow paths by the passage of countless scaled bellies. A carved full moon looks down from the ceiling. Open doorways lead north, south and west, and the east door is locked, its keyhole set in a bronze plate shaped like a waning moon.

L2:D2.name: Dripping Chamber
L2:D2.description: Water beads on the ceiling of this eastern chamber and drips onto tiles filmed with jelly-like slime, and the little blobs of it seem to hop and quiver when no one is looking. Rows of blocks divide the floor into narrow aisles that smell of damp. A locked door with a keyhole leads west, and the north wall is threaded with fine cracks that look ready to give to a bomb.

L2:C3.name: Gouged Hall
L2:C3.description: Curving gouges mark the walls of this chamber, and the floor is littered with chips of blue stone knocked loose by boomerangs hurled hard and often by doglike hands. Pairs of blocks flank the middle. An open doorway leads south, a locked door bars the east, and a heavy iron shutter fills the doorway north until the room falls quiet.

L2:D3.name: Cracked Eastern Room
L2:D3.description: A narrow eastern room whose walls are fractured top and bottom, the cracks wide enough to let a cold draught whisper through, as though bombs have been set off here before. Faint slime trails glisten across the floor and dry into crusts along the baseboards. A locked door leads west, while the north and south walls look thin and hollow.

L2:C4.name: Long Hall of the Moon
L2:C4.description: This chamber is part of the long north-south spine of the dungeon, its blue walls rising unbroken to a shadowed vault carved with the phases of the moon. Slither marks cross the dusty floor in lazy curves between the blocks, then snap straight toward the doors. A heavy shutter seals the south, and open doorways lead north and east.

L2:D4.name: Eastern Hall of Cuts
L2:D4.description: Deep, curving cuts score the walls of this room, sharper and longer than any wooden boomerang could make, and a scatter of broken masonry lies near the center. Four blue statues stand in the corners with mouths scorched black. The air smells of oiled leather, and a faint whirring echo circles the ceiling. An open doorway leads west; the north and south walls are veined with cracks.

L2:C5.name: Silent Chamber
L2:C5.description: An empty, silent chamber of pale blue stone, its floor swept bare and its corners deep in shadow. No track marks the dust here, and every footstep rings loud off the walls and comes back a moment late. A crescent moon is cut into the floor at the center. Open doorways lead north, south and east along the dungeon's long spine.

L2:D5.name: Trap-Grooved Room
L2:D5.description: Polished grooves cut across the floor of this cramped eastern room, running wall to wall where a spiked blade slides on its own the moment anything crosses its path. Bat droppings stain the upper ledges, and the air is stale. An open doorway leads west, and the north and south walls are both cracked and hollow-sounding, waiting for a bomb.

L2:C6.name: Serpent Hall
L2:C6.description: Coiled tracks and shed skins cover the floor of this long chamber, and the air is warm and close with reptile musk. A double row of stone blocks runs down its middle like a colonnade, and the furrows in the dust shoot straight along the lanes between them. An open doorway leads south, a locked door bars the east, and a heavy shutter stands to the north.

L2:D6.name: Slime-Pooled Cell
L2:D6.description: Glistening smears of slime trail across this small chamber, pooling in the grout between the tiles and dripping from the lip of the blocks, where tiny dark blobs of jelly cling. The walls are close and clammy. An open doorway leads north, a locked door with a keyhole leads west, and the south wall is laced with fine cracks.

L2:C7.name: Smoke-Stained Antechamber
L2:C7.description: Gouged walls and scattered stone chips mark this chamber below the dungeon's northern end. A low rumble comes from beyond the north wall, and the air smells of smoke and powder. Someone has scratched a warning beside the north door: DODONGO DISLIKES SMOKE. Heavy shutters stand north and south, and the east wall is split by a web of cracks.

L2:D7.name: Moonlit Smoke Hollow
L2:D7.description: Blue stone closes in on this northeast hollow, damp beading on every block, but the far end is dry and warm where a pair of fires burns low. Their smoke curls upward and gathers under the ceiling in a slow grey pall that never quite clears, and the floor between them is rubbed smooth. A crescent moon is scratched into one brazier's lip. An open doorway leads south, and the west wall is fractured and loose, held by old mortar.

L2:B8.name: Crescent Moon Sanctum
L2:B8.description: Quiet blue stone walls this sanctum in the dungeon's far northwest, a crescent moon carved above a triangle of gold leaf. A gentle golden light fills the air, and a triangle of light turns slowly in it, ready to bear the victor home. The hush is deep after the smoke next door. An iron-banded chest waits locked on the floor, and the door east, back to the lair, is locked with the moon's own key.

L2:C8.name: Dodongo's Lair
L2:C8.description: A broad, low chamber that stinks of smoke and scorched rock, its floor pitted with blast craters and pressed by huge three-toed footprints of a beast too thick-hided for any blade. Blackened scraps of fuse lie in the rubble. A heavy shutter seals the south door, and the door west is locked, a crescent moon around its keyhole.

L3:C1.name: Ooze Chamber
L3:C1.description: Thick, glistening puddles of slime spread across this square chamber, and the stone is stained a sickly green where they have dried. Some of the larger puddles quiver and split in two when disturbed. A pair of blocks stands near the middle, crusted at their bases. Open doorways lead east to the entrance and north into the dungeon.

L3:D1.name: Manji Gate
L3:D1.description: Green-tinged stone closes around this entrance hall, its walls carved with angular hooked patterns that turn in on themselves like the dungeon's own crooked plan. Cool, damp air rises from deeper within, smelling of moss and slime. A carved four-armed cross is set into the floor at the foot of the stair. The only doorway leads west.

L3:A2.name: Knight's Dead End
L3:A2.description: Heavy boot prints and the long scrape of armoured feet mar the dust in this far western chamber, and dents in the walls show where shields turned blows aside. Stone blocks stand in a loose ring, and one sits slightly out of line with the rest, its edges scuffed as though it has been shoved and a stair lies beneath. A heavy iron shutter seals the doorway north.

L3:C2.name: Streaked Hall
L3:C2.description: Long streaks of slime run down the walls of this hall, as if something heavy had tried to climb them and slid back down. The air is damp and smells of rot and wet stone, and the floor squelches in places where large green blobs have hopped. Open doorways lead north and south.

L3:A3.name: Armored Hall
L3:A3.description: Deep blade scratches line the walls of this western hall, and the floor is scuffed by heavy armoured steps that pace back and forth, always turning to face whoever enters. Squares of stone block lie in a checker pattern. An open doorway leads north, a locked door with a keyhole leads east, and a heavy shutter seals the south.

L3:B3.name: Hall of Blades
L3:B3.description: Smooth grooves cut along the walls of this chamber, worn deep by spiked traps that rest in all four corners and slam toward anything crossing their lines. Bat droppings speckle the floor in the lanes between them, and the ceiling rustles. Open doorways lead north and east, and a locked door with a keyhole stands to the west.

L3:C3.name: Manji Crossing
L3:C3.description: This is the heart of the dungeon's crooked cross, a broad chamber where halls meet from every side and the hooked carvings on the walls all point inward. Green slime pools in the low places between the worn floor tiles. Open doorways lead north, south and west, and the east wall is split by deep cracks that look ready to crumble under a bomb.

L3:D3.name: Eastern Slime Hall
L3:D3.description: Glistening sludge coats the floor of this chamber in thick, drying layers, and the smell of damp moss hangs heavy. A row of blocks lines the far wall. An open doorway leads north, a heavy iron shutter seals the east, and the west wall is fractured and sounds hollow when struck, as if bombs have been tried on it before.

L3:E3.name: Chamber of Cold Flickers
L3:E3.description: A creeping chill hangs in this small chamber, and pale blue flickers dance at the edge of sight before winking out, like a flaming skull bouncing from wall to wall. Those who brush against it say their sword arm goes numb. Bat droppings and shards of old bone lie across the stone. Heavy iron shutters seal both the north and the west doorways.

L3:A4.name: Haunted West Room
L3:A4.description: A dim chamber at the dungeon's western reach, where eerie flickers of light wink in the corners and vanish when looked at directly, and bats chitter in the rafters. Bat droppings crust the ledges, and the air is cold and thin. Open doorways lead east and south.

L3:B4.name: Bat Gallery
L3:B4.description: The ceiling of this chamber is pocked with crevices where bats roost, and the floor beneath is stained with their droppings. Two blocks stand near the center, chipped by claws, and a hooked Manji carving is cut deep into each. Open doorways lead west and south, and a locked door with a keyhole bars the east.

L3:C4.name: Hall of Three Locks
L3:C4.description: Locked doors stand on three sides of this chamber, north, east and west, each with a heavy keyhole set in iron, and only the southern arch stands open. Slime smears glisten across the floor and dry to a green crust along the base of the walls, and the hooked carvings on each door seem to turn the eye from one to the next.

L3:D4.name: Room of Sliding Blades
L3:D4.description: Four spiked traps rest in the corners of this chamber, and the floor between them is cut with straight, polished grooves where they slam together. An open doorway leads south and a locked door leads west. The east wall is cracked from floor to ceiling, and a sweet, green smell like a monstrous flower seeps through the fissures.

L3:E4.name: Manhandla's Lair
L3:E4.description: Thick vines and torn, fleshy petals carpet this chamber, heavy with the sweetness of a monstrous four-headed bloom. Whip-marks and scorch spots score the floor, and the walls are pitted where the plant rammed itself, faster each time a head was cut away. A shutter seals the south, the west wall is cracked, and the door north is locked with the guardian's key.

L3:C5.name: Manji Hall of Grinding Grooves
L3:C5.description: Twin grooves cut across this narrow chamber of green stone, and spiked blades rest at their ends against the walls, poised to slide at the first footstep and grind back afterwards. The floor between them is scored with fresh, bright scratches and dusted with iron filings that glitter in the torchlight. A locked door leads south, and a heavy iron shutter seals the doorway north.

L3:E5.name: Sanctum of the Golden Cross
L3:E5.description: A turning cross inlaid in gold marks the centre of this quiet chamber above the lair, and warm golden light hangs in the air around it. The green stone is clean, untouched by slime or vine, and a small triangle of light spins over the cross, a road home for whoever has earned it. An iron-banded chest stands locked on the cross, and the door south, back into the overgrown lair, is locked with the guardian's key.

L3:B6.name: Northwest Roost
L3:B6.description: Shadows crowd the high corners of this quiet chamber, and the musk of roosting bats hangs thick in the air. Droppings stain the tiles in long pale streaks, and wings stir faintly overhead, darting and pausing in no pattern at all. A heavy iron shutter seals the eastern doorway, the only way in or out.

L3:C6.name: Manji Hearth Chamber
L3:C6.description: Green stone gives way here to a floor of fitted slate, swept clean in a wide square around two braziers set against the north wall. The fires crackle with a cheerful popping, and amber light runs along a frieze of turning crosses carved just below the ceiling. A threadbare mat lies between the flames, flattened by long use. Heavy iron shutters seal the south and west doorways.

L3:cellar:A2.name: Pitch-Scented Cellar
L3:cellar:A2.description: Cramped and cool, this brick basement is laid out in narrow ledges over dark gaps, and it smells of wet timber and pitch. Water drips somewhere unseen below, and bat droppings spot the ledges. A stone shelf in the gloom at the far end is where the dungeon's keeper hides his coin, its edge rubbed smooth by a careful hand. The ladder leads back up.

L4:A1.name: Dripping Roost
L4:A1.description: A cramped chamber of damp blue stone opens off the entry hall to the east. It is dark here, the kind of dark a candle is made for, and bat droppings streak the floor beneath cracks in the ceiling. The steady drip of lake water echoes from somewhere overhead, and the air is thick with mildew and the sour reek of guano.

L4:B1.name: Mouth of the Snake
L4:B1.description: The entry hall of the Snake lies beneath its lake island, walls of glistening blue-green brick carved with coiling serpents whose tails wind away into the dark. Cold, wet air breathes up from the depths to the north, and a low side opening leads west into a blacker room. Behind, the stair climbs back toward daylight and the lap of lake water on the shore.

L4:B2.name: Moat Crossing
L4:B2.description: A channel of dark, still water cuts across this hall, crossed by a raised strip of flagstones. Long gouges near the doorways show where something heavy, armoured and shielded paces, always turning its face to the intruder, and torn wing membrane drifts on the water. A locked door with a brass keyhole is set in the east wall, while open ways lead north and south.

L4:C2.name: Serpent Coil Chamber
L4:C2.description: Blocks are laid across the floor in a slow spiral, like the coils of a great snake turning toward the center of the room, and the darkness between them swallows lamplight. Talon scratches mark the upper walls where winged, hopping things cling and scraps of bat wing lie where they burst apart. The only way out is the locked door in the west wall, its keyhole furred with green corrosion.

L4:A3.name: Lane of Blocks
L4:A3.description: Two rows of squat stone blocks march down the length of this dark chamber, leaving a narrow lane between them. The vaulted ceiling is cracked and stained by seepage, and dark claw marks score the plaster near its peak where something blue-winged hops and perches. Openings lead east and north.

L4:B3.name: Seeping Gallery
L4:B3.description: Water oozes from the mortar in long green stains and gathers in shallow hollows across the floor, black in the unlit gloom. Fluttering echoes and a litter of droppings betray a roost in the dark vault above, where wings dart and pause. The way out lies south, with a second opening to the west.

L4:A4.name: Still Corridor
L4:A4.description: A long, hushed hall lies quiet but for the sound of water moving behind its walls. Carved snake heads jut from each corner, their stone tongues worn smooth by centuries of damp, and their eyes seem to follow anyone who passes. Puddles on the floor ripple faintly whenever the lake shifts above. Passages open north and south.

L4:A5.name: Crackling Antechamber
L4:A5.description: Faint blue sparks crackle and fade in the air of this chamber, leaving a sharp tang like an oncoming storm, and a flaming skull's glow flickers in the corners. Scraps of blue wing lie on the floor beside smaller black ones, as if each winged thing broke into two smaller ones when struck. To the north a locked door bars the way, its keyhole crusted with verdigris, and an open way leads south.

L4:B5.name: Hall of Biting Serpents
L4:B5.description: Wide flagstones stretch between walls carved with scaled serpents swallowing their own tails. A heavy iron shutter fills the east doorway, and to the north a door is fastened with a stout lock. Fresh scratches on the lintels hint at blue-winged, horned things that perch above the doors and hop down onto whoever passes beneath.

L4:C5.name: Room of the Sunken Block
L4:C5.description: A broad moat of black water rings the middle of this chamber, and on the island it encloses one block sits a hair out of line with its fellows, a stair hinted beneath. Patches of sticky, glistening residue stain the flagstones near the water beside the torn straps of a swallowed shield. The only door, a heavy shutter, lies to the west.

L4:A6.name: Divided Hall
L4:A6.description: Rows of blocks split this chamber into narrow lanes running north to south, and the dark between them is deep enough to want a candle. A shutter of banded iron blocks the north door and a locked door guards the south, while the east side stands open. Torn scraps of leathery wing membrane lie scattered beneath the ledges.

L4:B6.name: Slick Chamber
L4:B6.description: Blobs of jelly-like slime glisten in the cracks between the flagstones and hop sluggishly in the dark, and the air carries a faintly sour smell. The north wall is crazed with hairline cracks around one thin, weak-looking section, and a glint of coin seems to show through. A locked door stands to the south and an open way leads west.

L4:A7.name: Cold Crossing
L4:A7.description: This bare chamber is hushed and cold, its floor broken only by a lone column of blocks carved with a single coiled snake. Shutters seal the north and south doorways, and the eastern wall shows a patch of crumbling, discoloured brick that a bomb would open. Water trickles unseen somewhere beneath the floor.

L4:B7.name: The Sealed Heart
L4:B7.description: A small chamber lies walled in on every side, with no proper door at all.
