shop:E4.description: Pushing the middle statue aside revealed a stair into this jewel-box of a shop, where blue light off a velvet cushion explains the gleam that shone from beneath the Armos. Two fires burn in polished braziers. On the counter a small Key bears a painted 80, the Blue Ring a painted 250, and a slab of bait a painted 60. Sand from the restless ground above sifts onto the steps leading up.

shop:E5.name: The Riverbank Powder Store
shop:E5.description: River damp creeps in at the mouth of this cave, so the goods are kept on raised boards well away from the walls. A pair of fires burn at a careful distance from the stock: a Magical Shield with 130 painted beneath it, a bundle of four bombs marked 20, and a quiver of arrows marked 80. Black powder dust greys the floor. Stairs lead up toward the river.

shop:F3.name: Fuse and Fletching
shop:F3.description: Petals from the spinning flowers outside have blown into this cave and caught among a litter of spent fuses and stray feathers. Two fires burn behind a counter of stacked crates. Displayed upon it are a Magical Shield priced 130, four bombs tied together with string priced 20, and a full quiver of arrows priced 80, the numbers brushed on in white paint. Stairs rise to the flowered field.

shop:G3.name: Polished Metal Shop
shop:G3.description: The glint seen through the cracks belongs to a row of burnished shields hanging on pegs, and the bomb that opened the bluff has left grit on every one of them. Two fires warm the room, and painted on a board above the counter are the prices: 90 for the Magical Shield, 100 for the bait, 10 for the Recovery Heart, each item set out beneath its number. The way up leads back to the meadow.

shop:G5.name: The Reedside Trading Post
shop:G5.description: Wet steps beneath the burned reedside bush are smeared with ash, and the stone with the painted mark turns out to be the top of a stair. Below, a cool cave smells of lake mud and lamp oil. Two fires light three wares on a driftwood plank: a Magical Shield over a daubed 90, bait over 100, and a Recovery Heart over 10. Reeds are bundled in a corner for kindling. Stairs climb up to the bank.

shop:G7.name: The Waxlight Shop
shop:G7.description: Drips of old wax have built up on every ledge of this cave into pale, lumpy spires, and the warm smell of tallow is thick enough to taste. Two fires and a dozen candle stubs light the goods: a Magical Shield painted 160, a small Key painted 100, and a Blue Candle painted 60, its wick already trimmed. Scattered pebbles from the slope have rolled in by the door. Stairs climb up onto the knoll.

shop:K5.name: Ledge-Shadowed Armoury
shop:K5.description: Beneath the overhanging ledge the cave is cool and cramped, with stone shelves cut right into the rock. Two fires burn in a pit lined with sand, well away from a shelf of black-powder bombs bundled in fours under a painted 20. Beside them hang a quiver of arrows marked 80 and a Magical Shield marked 130. Blue lichen tracked in from outside streaks the floor. Steps climb up to the rise.

shop:M1.name: The Lampsmoke Cave
shop:M1.description: Soot from years of lamp smoke has blackened the ceiling of this cave so thoroughly that it looks like night overhead. Dust from the hollow is tracked well inside, and the two fires are kept small to save fuel. On a slab counter sit a Magical Shield beneath a painted 160, a small Key beneath 100, and a Blue Candle beneath 60, with spare wicks coiled beside it. The way out is up the stair.

shop:N5.name: The Crossroads Cellar Shop
shop:N5.description: Charred twigs from the burned bush crackle on the stair down to this cellar shop, whose shield caught the light from above. Inside, two fires burn and the walls are hung with blue hide stretched to dry. Goods sit on an old door laid across two barrels: a Magical Shield painted 90, a cut of bait painted 100, and a Recovery Heart painted 10. Stairs climb back to the crossroads.

shop:O6.name: Wick and Tallow Den
shop:O6.description: At the end of the forest trail this cave keeps its candlelight steady, sheltered from every draught by the shoulder of rock. Rows of hardened tallow drips hang from a beam like icicles. Two fires burn at the back, and laid on a bench are a Magical Shield with 160 painted above it, a small Key with 100, and a Blue Candle with 60. A worn stair climbs up to the hollow among the trees.

shop:P7.name: The Salt-Air Arsenal
shop:P7.description: Sea air has followed the cave mouth inward, leaving a crust of salt on the stone and a tang mixed with lamp oil and black powder. Driftwood shelves hold the stock beside two fires: a Magical Shield with 130 painted on the wood beneath it, four bombs bound with tarred cord at 20, and a quiver of arrows at 80. Gull feathers in the fletching suggest local work. Steps rise to the bluffs.

potion_shop:D4.name: Apothecary in the Bluff
potion_shop:D4.description: Shards of the bombed bluff lie just inside, and beyond it the cave smells strongly of boiled roots and bitter tonic. Bundles of herbs hang from cords strung between the walls, and two fires keep a small kettle simmering. On a shelf stand two painted prices, 40 below a blue Life Potion and 68 below a red one, though nothing here is sold without sight of the royal letter. Stairs lead up past the rubble.

potion_shop:E1.name: The Herbwife's Cave
potion_shop:E1.description: The swept threshold gives way to a cave hung with drying leaves, mushroom caps and knotted roots, and the bitter smell of medicine fills it end to end. Two fires burn beneath a pair of iron pots, one tinted blue, one red. A ledge carries the painted prices, 40 for the blue Life Potion and 68 for the red 2nd Potion, beside a stone tray where a royal letter is laid to be read. The way out climbs up to the ledge.

potion_shop:E7.name: Simmering Herb Cellar
potion_shop:E7.description: Mist from the Lost Woods creeps down the steps and mingles with the steam of simmering herbs, so that the cave seems full of a sour green fog. A pair of fires heat a broad copper pan, and the walls are crowded with jars of powdered bark. Painted on a slate are two prices, 40 for a blue Life Potion and 68 for a red 2nd Potion, served only to one bearing the princess's letter. Steps lead up into the woods.

potion_shop:H3.name: Dispensary at the Mountain's Foot
potion_shop:H3.description: Crumbled outcrop stone litters the floor of this narrow dispensary, and the bitter herbal smell that leaked through the cracks is overwhelming inside. A mortar and pestle sit on a stump between two fires, stained dark from grinding. Small flasks stand in a rack with painted prices, a blue Life Potion at 40 and a red 2nd Potion at 68, kept for bearers of the princess's letter. The way out is up through the broken rock.

potion_shop:I8.name: The Root-Brewer's Hollow
potion_shop:I8.description: Crushed leaves and ash from the burned bush mix on the steps, and the medicine smell grows sharper with every step down. The hollow is round and low, warmed by twin fires, with a long table carrying cloth bags of dried flowers and a scale for weighing them. Beside a blue and a red bottle the prices are painted, 40 and 68; both are held back for a bearer of the princess's letter. Stairs climb to the meadow.

potion_shop:L5.name: Thicket Medicine Cellar
potion_shop:L5.description: Below the scorched roots of the burned bush a cellar opens, lined with shelves of corked bottles that clink whenever someone walks overhead. The air is sweet and bitter at once, the smell of medicine left too long on the boil. Two fires burn at the back. Painted on the shelf edge are 40 for a blue Life Potion and 68 for a red 2nd Potion, sold only on sight of the princess's letter. Stairs lead up into the thicket.

potion_shop:N1.name: The Draughty Remedy Shop
potion_shop:N1.description: The draught that whispered out of the cliff seams blows freely through the bombed opening now, stirring dried herbs on their pegs and carrying a medicinal reek over the heights. Two fires burn in a hearth against the far wall. Two clay tiles carry painted prices, 40 for the blue Life Potion and 68 for the red 2nd Potion, for bearers of the princess's letter only. The way out climbs up through the shattered cliff.

door_repair:B1.name: The Patched Ridge Door
door_repair:B1.description: The bomb that opened this place did not go unnoticed: the doorway is already fitted with a mended door of rough planks, its hinges fresh and its frame packed with mortar still damp to the touch. Inside, two fires burn and a slate on the wall tallies repairs in neat strokes. A tin cup by the threshold waits for twenty rupees from each newcomer. The way up leads back to the ridge.

door_repair:D1.name: The Mason's Grievance
door_repair:D1.description: Brittle stone flakes still lie inside the entrance, swept into a neat pile beside a newly mended door made of slate slabs pinned with iron. The room past it is bare except for two fires and a ledger on a ledge, its last entries a running list of what the repairs have cost. Every so often a stone from the crest above thuds on the roof. A stair climbs up to the rockfall crest.

door_repair:D7.name: The Scorched Trapdoor
door_repair:D7.description: A trapdoor once lay hidden beneath the bramble bush, and the fire that burned the bush away blistered its planks black. It has been mended already, with new boards nailed over the scorch. Below it a small room holds two fires, a pot of nails and a hammer laid neatly on a shelf, with a bowl waiting for the twenty-rupee charge. Steps rise through the mended trapdoor to the brambles.

door_repair:E2.name: The Shored-Up Scarp Room
door_repair:E2.description: Timber props hold up the cracked ceiling of this room, whose floor was cleared by shovelling the scarp's rubble aside. A mended door of split logs hangs in the opening, its new latch bright against the old wood. Two fires warm the room, and a clay jar on the floor rattles with the coins already taken in payment for the work. The way out is up the rubble stair to the scarp.

door_repair:H1.name: The Summit Repair Room
door_repair:H1.description: The crack that ran down the cliff has been turned into a doorway and then shut again by a mended door of iron-banded oak, braced against the summit winds. Scorch marks from fiery breath outside reach a little way in. The room holds two fires, a coil of rope, and a bucket of mortar with a trowel stuck in it, beside an empty dish for the fee. The stair climbs back up to the summit road.

door_repair:I7.name: Under the Hedge Doorframe
door_repair:I7.description: The new-looking doorframe glimpsed between the bush roots holds a mended door, painted green to match the hedge before the fire took that part of it away. Ash still powders its top. Through it lies a neat square room with two fires, a broom, and a wooden plate nailed beside the frame where twenty rupees are laid down. The stair beyond the door goes up to the field.

door_repair:K7.name: The River-Damp Repair Shop
door_repair:K7.description: Grey paste coats the damp steps where ash from the burned riverbank bush met the river mist, and the mended door at their foot is swollen with river mist, its new boards paler than the old. The room inside smells of wet sawdust. Two fires burn on a raised hearth to keep the floor dry, and a ledger lies open on a stool, every line of it reading twenty. Steps climb back to the thicket.

door_repair:N8.name: Seaside Mended Door
door_repair:N8.description: The boom of the sea carries faintly through the rock into this room, whose blasted entrance now wears a mended door made of salvaged ship planks, still crusted with salt. Rubble has been stacked into a low bench along one wall. Two fires burn in the middle of the floor, and a scallop shell set on the bench holds the twenty-rupee charge of whoever came before. A stair leads up to the shore path.

door_repair:O2.name: Behind the Gouged Cliff
door_repair:O2.description: Light that once showed between the cracks now leaks around the edges of a hastily mended door, its planks fitted unevenly into the gouged cliff. Chips of rock from the blast crunch underfoot. Two fires burn low near a stack of spare boards, and an upturned helmet by the fires serves as the collection box for the twenty rupees every visitor owes for the damage. Stairs lead up to the cliffs.

gamble:A2.name: The Gorge Gaming Den
gamble:A2.description: Broken gorge rock has been kicked into a corner to make room for the game. Three rupee markers sit in a straight row on the swept floor, painted alike so that nothing tells them apart, and two fires throw their glow across them. The wind howling through the gorge outside can be heard faintly. Scuffs before the markers show where players have paid their ten. The way out climbs up through the broken wall.

gamble:G2.name: The Wager Room
gamble:G2.description: Every time a rock bounces down the gully outside, the three rupee markers laid on the floor of this room jump a little and settle again. The clinking heard through the cracks is plain now: stacks of coin are piled near the two fires, waiting to be won or swallowed at ten a try. A line scratched before the markers shows where a player stands to choose. Gravel from the blast covers the stair up to the gully.

gamble:G8.name: Dice Rattle Cavern
gamble:G8.description: Behind the cracked crag face, the rattle heard outside turns out to be a cup of dice left on a ledge, a toy beside the real game. Three rupee markers lie spaced evenly across the floor between two fires, each one a gamble that might fatten a ten-rupee stake or empty a purse. Hard-packed dirt before them is worn smooth by nervous feet. The stair leads up through the blasted rock to the crags.

gamble:M8.name: Sandblown Gambling Cave
gamble:M8.description: Dune sand keeps finding its way in through the bombed entrance, and it has drifted around the three rupee markers set out on the floor so that only their tops show. Two fires burn behind them. The stacked coins heard from outside sit in towers of different heights, winnings and losses side by side. Ten small notches cut into the floor mark the price of a turn. A sandy stair rises to the dunes.

gamble:P2.name: The Cliffside Game Parlour
gamble:P2.description: Morning light from the cliff shelf reaches only a little way into this cave before the glow of two fires takes over. Three rupee markers lie in a row on a strip of faded red carpet, and a battered cup sits beside a heap of coins where the laughter and rattling came from. The floor before the carpet is scuffed by countless visitors who stopped to try their luck at ten a turn. Stairs lead up to the shelf.

warp_hall:D3.name: The Western Crossway
warp_hall:D3.description: The scraped earth under the moved boulder gives onto a long hall, cool and echoing, its far side pierced by three stairways set at even distances, west, centre and east. Each descends into darkness that smells faintly of somewhere else, grass in one, sand in another, water in the third. Two fires burn at the hall's midpoint. The way back climbs up to the boulder and the trampled grass.

warp_hall:J5.name: Hall Beneath the Meadow Stone
warp_hall:J5.description: A draught pours up from below the moved stone and runs the length of this hall, setting the two fires leaning. Three stairways open in the floor along the far side, one to the west, one in the centre and one to the east, each with its steps worn by travellers who chose and were carried far away. Turf roots hang from the ceiling near the entrance. Stairs climb up into the boulder meadow.

warp_hall:J8.name: The Southern Warp Gallery
warp_hall:J8.description: Fresh-turned earth from beneath the great stone has spilled down onto the first steps of this gallery. It is long and plain, built of dressed grey blocks, and three stairways break its floor at the west end, the centre and the east end, each one a road to a distant part of Hyrule. A pair of fires lights the gallery from its centre. The way out is up to the stone field.

warp_hall:N2.name: Frost-Rimed Crossroads Hall
warp_hall:N2.description: High in the mountains, the hall under the heavy boulder is colder than its kin, frost glittering on the stone near the entrance. Three stairways open in a row along its length, west, centre and east, and wind breathes out of each one carrying the scent of some lowland far away. Two fires burn steadily despite the chill, their smoke drawn down the stairways. The way out climbs up to the high meadow.
